topics: 🔄 A Tradition Reversed — Rav Mordekhai and Rav Ashi disagree about who said what regarding wilderness sanctity
🔢 Kontrokos's Two Puzzles — the missing 300 Levites and Moses's 'missing' Tabernacle silver
🐴 Why Donkeys Alone? — Rabbi Eliezer on the Exodus donkeys, plus digressions on Rephidim and Shittim
🐮 New Mishna: Cross-Species Birth — a cow birthing a donkey-like creature, and the kashrut rule that follows the mother
📜 Two Sources for 'Must Resemble Its Mother' — the mishna's tanna and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili trade derivations

overview.title: 📖 Overview: From Wilderness Accounting to a New Mishna
overview.subtitle: Bekhorot 5a–5b
overview.hebrewSource: פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר... פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר, שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf closes out the wilderness-sanctity debate with a twist: different academies transmitted the Rabbi Yoḥanan–Reish Lakish dispute in opposite directions. It then records the Roman officer Kontrokos's two sharp arithmetic challenges to Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, and Rabbi Ḥanina's question to Rabbi Eliezer about why only donkeys, among non-kosher animals, require redemption. A new mishna then opens fresh territory: when a cow gives birth to a donkey-like creature, or a donkey to a horse-like one, is the offspring subject to firstborn redemption, and may it be eaten?

slides.title: 🔄 Whose Opinion Is It? A Tradition Reversed
slides.subtitle: Rav Mordekhai tells Rav Ashi they learned the dispute backward

lines.speaker: Rav Mordekhai
lines.text: You have it backward! We teach: Rabbi Yoḥanan says firstborns were not sanctified in the wilderness, and Reish Lakish says they were.

lines.speaker: Rav Ashi
lines.text: Then do you also reverse Rabbi Elazar's proof — the one he attributed to Rabbi Yoḥanan after seeing him in a dream?

lines.speaker: Rav Mordekhai
lines.text: No — in my version, 'not sanctified' means they didn't need separate consecration, since they were already holy. The practical outcome matches your version exactly.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: So why report it in reversed language at all? To teach: a student must state a ruling in his teacher's own precise wording.

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: Two schools reached identical halakha through mirror-image terminology — a lesson about transmitting Torah faithfully, word for word.

slides.title: 🔢 Kontrokos's Two Puzzles for Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai
slides.subtitle: A Roman officer challenges the wilderness census and Temple accounting
rows: Individual Levite families total 22,300, but the collective count is only 22,000 (Numbers 3:39) — where did 300 go?
They were themselves firstborn Levites; a firstborn cannot abrogate another firstborn's sanctity — it suffices for him to abrogate his own
Silver collected totaled 201 talents + 11 maneh, but only 100 talents were used for casting the sockets — 'was Moses a thief?'
Moses was a trustworthy treasurer: the Sanctuary's maneh was double a standard maneh (50 shekels, not 25), so the sums match exactly

callout.label: Underlying principle:
callout.text: A community may increase standard measures, but never by more than one-sixth — calculated from the final, increased total.

slides.title: 🐴 Why Donkeys, and Not Horses or Camels?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Ḥanina's questions to Rabbi Eliezer 'in the great study hall'

steps.content: 1️⃣ Question: why are firstborn donkeys redeemed with a lamb, while firstborn horses and camels are not redeemed at all?
2️⃣ Answer: it is a Torah decree — and besides, donkeys assisted Israel at the Exodus, each family leaving Egypt with ninety superior donkeys laden with silver and gold
3️⃣ Follow-up: what does the place-name 'Rephidim' mean? Rabbi Eliezer: simply its name. (Rabbi Yehoshua elsewhere: it alludes to Israel growing lax [ריפיון] in Torah study there)
4️⃣ Follow-up: and 'Shittim'? Rabbi Eliezer: simply its name. (Rabbi Yehoshua: it alludes to Israel's involvement in 'foolish' [שְׁטוּת] matters — idolatry and licentiousness there)

callout.label: Pattern:
callout.text: Rabbi Eliezer consistently reads place-names literally; Rabbi Yehoshua elsewhere reads them as moral allusions to what happened there.

slides.title: 🐮 New Mishna: When Mother and Offspring Differ in Species
slides.subtitle: Redemption and kashrut rules for cross-species births

boxes.title: Cow → Donkey-like Offspring
items: 'Firstborn of a donkey...firstborn of a donkey' stated twice (Exodus 13:13, 34:20) requires both mother and offspring to be a donkey
Permitted to eat — a kosher mother's offspring is kosher regardless of appearance

boxes.title: Donkey → Horse-like Offspring
items: Neither animal is eaten, so no separate kashrut question arises here

boxes.title: General Kashrut Rule
items: Kosher animal births a non-kosher-looking creature: permitted to eat
Non-kosher animal births a kosher-looking creature: forbidden to eat
Status always follows the mother, never the offspring's appearance

slides.title: 📜 Two Sources for 'Must Resemble Its Mother'
slides.subtitle: The mishna's tanna and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derive the same rule from opposite directions

lines.speaker: Our tanna
lines.text: I learn 'donkey mother, donkey offspring' from the doubled donkey verses. Since the Torah revealed this for a donkey's value-sanctity, the same applies to a kosher animal's inherent sanctity.

lines.speaker: R' Yosei HaGelili
lines.text: I learn it the other way: from the doubled 'firstborn...firstborn' by ox, lamb, and goat (Numbers 18:17). Since the Torah revealed it for inherent sanctity, the same applies to a donkey's value-sanctity.

lines.speaker: Our tanna
lines.text: Then what do I do with the ox/lamb/goat repetition? I use it to teach that sacrificial portions are burned on the altar for each of the three species separately — none could be derived from the other two.

lines.speaker: R' Yosei HaGelili
lines.text: And I use the doubled donkey verse differently: to exclude firstborn horses and camels from redemption altogether — only a donkey's firstborn is redeemed with a lamb.

callout.label: Same rule, opposite proofs:
callout.text: Both agree the offspring must match its mother's species; they disagree only about which case — donkey or kosher animal — is the primary source.

summary.principle: Firstborn status requires the offspring to match its mother's species, derived from doubled verses on both sides of the Torah's firstborn laws; meanwhile, only donkeys among non-kosher animals require redemption, a decree tied to their service at the Exodus.

flowSteps.content: 🔄 Two schools transmit the wilderness-sanctity dispute in opposite terms, yet reach the same halakha
🔢 Kontrokos's puzzles resolved: firstborn Levites don't count as redeemers; the Sanctuary's maneh was double the standard

columns.content: 🐴 Donkeys alone are redeemed among non-kosher animals — a decree tied to their role at the Exodus
🐮 New mishna: mother and offspring must match species; kashrut always follows the mother

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: firstborn redemption requires the offspring to resemble its mother's species — proven from doubled verses for both donkeys and kosher animals

quiz.q: According to Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, why does the individual Levite family count (22,300) exceed the collective total of 22,000 used to redeem Israelite firstborns?
o: It was a scribal error in the Torah
The extra 300 were themselves firstborn Levites, and a firstborn cannot abrogate another firstborn's sanctity
The extra 300 were counted twice by mistake
They were Levite women, who were not included
quiz.e: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai explained that 300 Levites were firstborns themselves; a firstborn Levite can only abrogate his own firstborn sanctity, not another's.

quiz.q: How does Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai resolve the apparent gap between the 201 talents of silver collected and only 100 talents used for the Tabernacle sockets?
o: Moses kept the difference for himself
The Sanctuary's maneh was worth double a standard maneh, so the totals actually match
The extra silver was lost in transit
The verse contains a printing error
quiz.e: He explained that a maneh of the Sanctuary equaled 50 shekels rather than the standard 25, making the accounts balance precisely — Moses was a trustworthy and expert treasurer.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Eliezer, why are firstborn donkeys redeemed while firstborn horses and camels are not?
o: Horses and camels are kosher animals
It is a Torah decree, and donkeys also assisted Israel at the Exodus by carrying Egypt's silver and gold
Horses and camels did not exist in ancient Israel
Donkeys are the only non-kosher animals mentioned in the Torah
quiz.e: Rabbi Eliezer cites both a straightforward Torah decree and the merit of donkeys, which carried the wealth of Egypt for the Israelites at the Exodus.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, why is a cow's donkey-like offspring exempt from firstborn-donkey redemption?
o: Because cows never give birth to donkeys in reality
Because the Torah states 'firstborn of a donkey' twice, requiring both the mother and the offspring to be a donkey
Because only male offspring are subject to redemption
Because the mishna exempts all unusual births
quiz.e: The doubled phrase 'firstborn of a donkey...firstborn of a donkey' (Exodus 13:13, 34:20) teaches that firstborn-donkey status requires the mother to be a donkey AND the offspring to be a donkey.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, what determines whether an animal born looking unlike its mother is permitted to eat?
o: The offspring's own appearance
The mother's kashrut status, regardless of the offspring's appearance
Whichever status is more lenient
It depends on the day of the week it was born
quiz.e: The mishna rules that what emerges from a non-kosher animal is non-kosher, and what emerges from a kosher animal is kosher — status always follows the mother, not the offspring's looks.
